summary:
MISSION ECHO is an interactive educational game designed for children aged 7–12 to learn about Mars exploration. In this game, players take the role of a Commander and are guided by a friendly astronaut companion named Echo to complete four missions on Mars.

I developed four missions based on real NASA science and Mars exploration. Players will explore Gale Crater and Curiosity rover discoveries, learn about radiation and astronaut protection, discover how plants can be grown in space, and understand how NASA's MOXIE experiment produced oxygen from the carbon dioxide-rich Martian atmosphere.

The game addresses the challenge by turning space science information into interactive activities. Instead of only reading facts, players can explore discovery panels, make decisions, complete challenges, and manage three important resources: Oxygen, Power, and Food. These activities help children understand some of the challenges that astronauts may face when exploring Mars. The game is also available in English and Bahasa Melayu to make learning more accessible.

This project is important because learning about space can be difficult for children when scientific information is presented in a complex way. Through MISSION ECHO, I hope to make Mars exploration easier to understand, more interesting, and more engaging. It also encourages children to think, make decisions, ask questions, and develop an interest in science and space exploration.
details:
1. What does the project do and how does it work?

MISSION ECHO is an interactive educational game designed for children aged 7–12 to learn about Mars exploration. Players take the role of a Commander and are guided by a friendly astronaut companion named Echo throughout four missions on Mars.

The game consists of four Sol missions. In Sol 1, players explore Gale Crater and learn about Curiosity rover discoveries. In Sol 2, they learn about radiation and the importance of protecting astronauts. In Sol 3, they discover how plants can be grown in space. In Sol 4, they learn about NASA's MOXIE experiment and how it produced oxygen from the carbon dioxide-rich Martian atmosphere.

Throughout the missions, players explore information panels, complete activities, make decisions and manage three resources: Oxygen, Power and Food. Their decisions affect the available resources and mission outcomes. The game also includes a mission review and completion system so players can revisit what they have learned.

2. The benefits of the project

The main benefit of MISSION ECHO is that it makes learning about Mars exploration more interactive and easier to understand. Instead of only reading scientific information, children can explore different topics and participate in activities.

It also introduces children to real NASA missions, scientific experiments and technologies. The game encourages decision-making, critical thinking and curiosity about science. In addition, having both English and Bahasa Melayu makes the learning experience more accessible to children.

3. The intended impact

I hope MISSION ECHO can encourage more children to become interested in space science and understand some of the challenges involved in exploring Mars.

Through the game, children can learn that exploring another planet requires more than just travelling there. Astronauts also need protection from radiation, food sources and ways to produce important resources such as oxygen.

My aim is to make children more curious about science, encourage them to ask questions and inspire them to explore more about space.

4. The tools and technologies

I developed this project using Google AI Studio Build with the assistance of Gemini AI. The application was developed using React and TypeScript, with TSX for the interface components.

I also used NASA and Canadian Space Agency educational resources as references for the scientific information and mission activities. NASA images and materials were included to help children understand the different Mars missions and technologies.

No special hardware was required because MISSION ECHO is designed as a web-based educational game.

5. How is the project creative?

The creative part of MISSION ECHO is the combination of space exploration, interactive learning and resource management in one educational game.

Instead of presenting four topics separately, I connected them through a Mars adventure where players take the role of a Commander. Echo acts as a companion who guides players through the missions.

I also included interactive discovery panels, decision-making activities, illustrative simulations and mission outcomes to make the learning experience more engaging. The bilingual feature allows children to explore the game in English or Bahasa Melayu.

6. What factors did I consider during development?

Since the target audience is children aged 7–12, I considered the difficulty of the scientific information, the simplicity of the activities and the overall user experience.

I wanted the game to be easy to navigate, with clear instructions and explanations. I also considered scientific accuracy by using NASA and Canadian Space Agency references instead of inventing scientific facts. Any fictional resource costs or illustrative simulations are presented as educational game elements rather than actual NASA measurements.

Another factor was accessibility. I included English and Bahasa Melayu, simple interactions and a friendly visual style to make the game more suitable for young learners.

7. Brainstorming and development process

I developed MISSION ECHO independently. During the brainstorming process, I explored different ways to turn Mars exploration topics into an educational game. I used ChatGPT to discuss ideas, organise the mission structure, evaluate possible activities and improve the learning experience.

I also used Gemini AI in Google AI Studio to assist with building the application and implementing its features. I reviewed the generated implementation, tested the activities and made adjustments to ensure the game worked as intended.

The project was developed step by step, starting with the main concept and welcome screen before moving on to the four missions and the overall adventure completion system.

8. Educational Approach and Learning Theories

MISSION ECHO was also designed with several educational learning approaches in mind. The game relates to Constructivism, where children develop their understanding through exploration, interaction and making decisions instead of only receiving information.

It also incorporates Experiential Learning, where players learn through activities, observe the outcomes of their decisions and reflect on what they have learned. For example, players manage Oxygen, Power and Food resources throughout the Mars missions and discover how their decisions affect the mission.

In addition, Echo acts as a learning companion by providing guidance, hints and explanations. This relates to the idea of scaffolding in Vygotsky's learning theory, where learners receive support to help them understand new concepts.

By combining these approaches, MISSION ECHO aims to create a learning experience where children can actively explore scientific information, make decisions and develop their understanding of Mars exploration.
